column1: # Golden vectors for gate_chain_verify — frozen (exit code, broken row) tuples.
# Each row: <case> <rcA> <brokeA> <rcB> <brokeB> <rcC> <brokeC>
# The three column pairs are NOT platform names. They are the three outcomes of
# one probe — what the `prev=` extractor returns for a row that carries an
# invalid UTF-8 byte — because that, not the vendor of `sed`, is what decides
# these verdicts:
#   A  the extractor yields nothing (it aborted, or matched nothing)
#      → the row updates no `prev` and the chain re-joins across it
#   B  the extractor yields exactly the hex the row carries
#      → the row is compared normally
#   C  the extractor yields something else non-empty
#      → the comparison is against a polluted value and cannot match
# Naming the observable instead of the vendor is what lets both CI legs assert a
# literal here. macOS/BSD `sed` measured as A on 2026-09-04; the ubuntu leg is
# expected to land on B or C, and whichever it is has a frozen expectation
# rather than a skip.
# `broke` is 0 when the chain verified. Row numbering counts every row-shaped
# line, including ones the extractor skipped — that is the existing convention
# and it is deliberately not changed.
# Derived by hand, then measured for column A. `prev=` digests in the ledgers are
# computed with openssl, never with the shasum the verifier itself uses.
# The five lines that moved when unreadable-`prev=` rows became a break are
# marked. Before that commit they read: insert-last-noprev 0 0 / 0 0 / 0 0,
# insert-last-badbytes 0 0, insert-mid-badbytes 0 0, replace-mid-badbytes 1 4
# (column A only), missing-ledger 0 0 / 0 0 / 0 0 — four of them a forged
# approval row or an unopened ledger passing as intact.
# `missing-ledger` reports broke=0 with rc=1: there is no row to point at,
# because nothing was read. That pair is the encoding of "not verified", which
# is a different statement from "verified and intact".
# Data lines carry NO trailing comment: the reader binds the last field to the
# rest of the line, so an inline note would be parsed as part of column C.
# replace-mid-badbytes now names row 3 — the row actually forged — where before
# it named row 4 and called it a splice.
identity                0 0   0 0   0 0
insert-last-noprev      1 5   1 5   1 5
insert-last-clean       1 5   1 5   1 5
insert-last-badbytes    1 5   1 5   1 5
insert-mid-clean        1 3   1 3   1 3
insert-mid-badbytes     1 3   1 3   1 3
replace-mid-clean       1 4   1 4   1 4
replace-mid-badbytes    1 3   1 4   1 3
missing-ledger          1 0   1 0   1 0
